newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Australia recognises Hong Kong's future passport.
newsitem.headline: Australia recognises Hong Kong's future passport.

text.p: Australia has agreed to recognise the passports that Hong Kong will issue after the territory reverts from British to Chinese rule on July 1, the Hong Kong government said on Thursday.

Australia has promised it will treat holders of the post-handover passports in the same way as holders of so-called British National Overseas (BNO) passports, which are held by about two million Hong Kong people, a government statement said.
BNO passport holders need a visa to enter Australia, but visa applications tend to be a formality.

A handful of countries -- including Britain, the United States, Canada, Singapore, Japan, the Philippines, and Western Samoa -- have recognised the territory's post-handover passport and announced favourable entry conditions ranging from easy visas to visa-free access.
